_comment: Reference data for tools/evidence_import.py (`intel.py evidence import <case> <findings.json>` / the evidence_import @tool). An analyst's graded findings are stored under cases/<case>/evidence/imported/ and written into the KB with the provenance tag below so assessments can cite them. Rung semantics come from rungs.json (owner = edge; kit / neighbour = fact only, RULE 5) — this file only holds the grading vocabulary and provenance labels. RULE 1: grading vocabulary only, never case data.

admiralty._comment: Admiralty (NATO) grade accepted on an imported finding: source reliability A-F + information credibility 1-6, e.g. B2. `pattern` is matched against the grade after upper-casing and stripping spaces / hyphens. A finding with no grade, or one that does not match, is REJECTED with a message — an ungraded claim cannot be cited.

reliability_confidence._comment: Source-reliability letter -> KB confidence word (knowledge_base.CONF_WORDS) for the facts and edges an imported finding writes. A/B are reliable sources, C fairly reliable, D-F not usually reliable / unreliable / cannot be judged.

provenance._comment: KB provenance labels: `source` is the tag every fact/edge carries (the harness assessment cites imported evidence by it); `collector` names this importer; `fact_attribute` is the attribute an indicator's finding is stored under; `default_rel` labels an owner selector_link that gave no rel.

attribute_rows._comment: Optional `attributes` rows on a finding ({entity, attribute, value, valid_from?, valid_until?}) set a KB attribute at the ANALYST authority tier (kb_memory.json), whatever the Admiralty grade (the grade only sets confidence). A single-valued attribute is reconciled — it supersedes, corrects or is disputed against the standing value; any other attribute is added as a plain analyst fact. `name_pattern` is the accepted attribute-name shape; `reserved` names belong to the importer and RULE 5 (link facts, rung labels) and are refused, so a row can never forge a kit/neighbour link or an analyst_finding.

finding_fields._comment: Optional per-finding report fields. `confirmation` is the analyst's confirmation level for the claim (an unknown value is dropped with a note; the finding still imports); `not_proven` is the boundary sentence — what the evidence does NOT show — rendered under the finding in the house report. Neither is ever written to the KB.

report_sections._comment: Schema of the optional top-level `report` block ({"findings": [...], "report": {...}}). Each key is a list of rows; a malformed row is REJECTED with a message and the rest import; an unknown key is rejected whole. `required` keys must be non-empty; `enums` are matched case-insensitively (priority upper-cased); `patterns` are regexes on the stripped value (case-sensitive); `dates` must be ISO-8601 (YYYY-MM-DD or a full date-time); `lists` accept a list of strings or one string; `numbers` must be JSON numbers; `raw_lists` are lists of strings/numbers stored as-is; `objects` are lists of sub-rows validated with their own spec; `dicts` are one JSON object of scalars (a value may be a list of scalars or one more flat object, never deeper) stored as-is; a duplicate `id` inside one import is rejected. Rows are stored inside the same content-addressed imported record and read back by tools/report_sections.py. RULE 5: report rows NEVER touch the KB — not even `roles`, which are analyst judgement for the report only, nor `metrics.values`, which may hold secrets and are kept only for the anti-inflation duplicate check (never printed in the report).

subject_profile._comment: Identity card rows. `entity` defaults to "subject". basis + source are REQUIRED on alias and relative rows (an unsourced alias / relative is how a wrong person enters a profile); other fields are linted, not rejected, when unsourced. Analyst judgement for the report only — never the KB (RULE 5).

client_seeds._comment: Details the CLIENT supplied at intake. Rendered in Methodology; sensitive=true values are withheld unless house_report --show-sensitive. Never the KB.

engagement._comment: ONE object (kind=object), not a list: document-control metadata for the report front matter. The latest import wins.

risk_assessment._comment: ONE object (kind=object): the C1 organisation risk object (exposure_score --model organisation writes the same shape to cases/<case>/exposure_organisation.json, read as the fallback). Rendered as the Executive Summary overall score + domain table and the Methodology 'Rating scales'. `dicts` are flat JSON objects stored as-is: overall {score, level, method, note}, coverage {rated, total, unrated[], note, warning}, bands {level: inclusive lower bound}, priorities {P1: deadline}. Unrated domains are omitted from `domains`.

key_findings._comment: Numbered key findings for the Executive Summary 'Key findings' table, used when the graded findings carry no priority. priority P1-P3 are the deadline buckets of risk_assessment.priorities; P4 is the Severity Tier Matrix 'track only' tier (no deadline; rendered 'P4 (track only — no deadline)') and is accepted HERE ONLY — roadmap stays P1-P3. A Critical / High row without a priority, and a Critical row at P4, are linted.

affiliate_exposure._comment: Infostealer exposure of affiliated organisations (subsidiaries, suppliers, partners). COUNTS ONLY: a row never carries a credential, cookie or password; extra keys are ignored by the renderer. stealer_family accepts one string or a list.

leak_claims._comment: Dark-web / Telegram claims naming the subject. proven=false renders as 'Unconfirmed' and feeds the 'Of N claims, K are proven' tally; a proven claim with no evidence is linted.

threat_events._comment: Upcoming events that raise the threat (summits, elections, product launches). An event whose end (else start) is before the report date is linted as stale.

usernames_to_reserve._comment: Person reports: handles to register defensively before an impersonator does.

negative_checks._comment: Checks that found nothing (court records, political donations, company directorships). Rendered with zero-hit sources under 'Checked — nothing found'; a negative result at collection time, not proof of absence.

email_services._comment: Person reports: services an e-mail address is registered with (account-existence evidence). The e-mail is withheld in the house report unless --show-sensitive.

relationships._comment: Person / organisation card map: one card per relation from the hub. `group` = panel title, `confirmed` false draws a dashed, unconfirmed card.

actors._comment: Threat card map: attackers by `type` (the panel title) around the case seed / brand. `confirmed` false = an unconfirmed claim, drawn dashed.

actor_profile._comment: ONE object (kind=object): the actor threat-profile deliverable (structure adapted from [PK Packt ACTIH companion repo, 2026, chapter-03 threat-profile deliverable], MIT). The latest import wins. `dicts` are flat objects stored as-is: attribution {assessment, likelihood (ICD-203 term), confidence, dissent[]}, intent {motivations[], evidence[]}, capability {summary, evidence[]}, victimology {sectors[], geographies[], data_targeted[]}. Optional strings: executive_line, tempo_summary, tempo_ref (pointer to the case timeline's tempo analysis), threat_score_ref (key into cases/<case>/actor_scores.json; default the name — the reader attaches `threat_score`). An attribution without a likelihood term or confidence, and an intent with no evidence, are linted. RULE 5: an analyst judgement and lead, never attribution in the KB or a same-operator edge.

claim_confidence._comment: Actor profile 'Source basis and confidence': one row per claim with the analyst's confidence and why. Low_to_Medium renders 'Low to Medium'. A High row without sources is linted.

pivot_opportunities._comment: Actor profile 'Infrastructure and defensive pivots': an artifact the defender holds, the question to pivot on, and what a hit is used for. A lead, never an edge.

playbook._comment: Actor profile 'Operational playbook': behaviours per ATT&CK tactic, rendered in tactic order (report_sections.json actor_profile.tactic_order). A row with attack_ids but no evidence is linted.

hunt_hypotheses._comment: Actor profile 'Hunt hypotheses' (HH-nn). hunt_package_ref is an optional key into the hunt-package index, carried as a string. A hypothesis without priority telemetry or behavioural signals is linted.

telemetry_priorities._comment: Actor profile 'Priority telemetry': the log sources a defender should hold to hunt this actor, in the analyst's priority order. baseline_ref is an optional key into IntelAnalysis/references/telemetry_baselines.json `settings` (the Windows audit setting that produces the source), carried as a string; one that does not resolve is linted.
